Home Depot Receipts
Keep Getting Bigger

lines.text: Fewer Home Depot trips. Bigger receipts. Here's why.
lines.say: Fewer Home Depot trips. Bigger receipts. Here's why.

lines.text: This morning Home Depot reported $43.4 billion in quarterly sales, up 4.9%.
lines.say: This morning, Home Depot reported forty-three point four billion dollars in quarterly sales, up four point nine percent.

lines.text: But look inside: comparable transactions fell 0.5%, while the average ticket rose 3.0%.
lines.say: But look inside: comparable transactions fell half a percent, while the average ticket rose three percent.

lines.text: The average receipt went from $90.39 to $93.09 in a year.
lines.say: The average receipt went from ninety dollars and thirty-nine cents to ninety-three dollars and nine cents in a year.

lines.text: And ticket growth has mostly sped up, from 1.8% a year ago to 3.0% now.
lines.say: And ticket growth has mostly sped up, from one point eight percent a year ago to three percent now.

lines.text: In February, the company tied bigger tickets to some price increases, pricier items and shoppers trading up.

post.title: Home Depot shoppers made fewer trips but paid more each time
post.ig:
Home Depot shoppers made fewer trips, but paid more each time.
Home Depot reported Q3 sales of $43.4 billion on Nov 17, 2026, up 4.9% from a year ago.
Comparable customer transactions fell 0.5%, while the comparable average ticket rose 3.0%.
The average receipt rose to $93.09 from $90.39. Comparable ticket growth has climbed from 1.8% a year ago.
Sources: The Home Depot Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings release (Nov 17, 2026); Home Depot Q4 fiscal 2025 earnings call (Feb 24, 2026).
